batch_strategy: Measure missing condition-response segments that distinguish transferable structure and loading effects from isolated endpoint anomalies. Combine targeted strong-eluent diagnostics, matched loading contrasts, and intermediate-ratio carbonyl comparisons, using existing measurements as anchors and avoiding incidental identical-input repeats.

choices.reason: m62 at 1/1, 50 uL tests transfer of the new 150-uL observation b3b38f7212d8649d9ac1, whose measured endpoints nearly coincide at 12.24/12.26 mL. The current 12.16/12.96 prediction extends that behavior across loading. This label distinguishes a reproducible ratio feature from an isolated observation.

m62 at 0/1, 50 uL pairs with its selected 1/1 row at unchanged loading. Prediction is 4.64/7.34 mL. Together with measured 150-uL endpoints 96b9b370ade7a60366fa and 2f907b475ae6a261a87a, it tests whether the apparent 1/1 maximum persists at lower loading without assuming monotonicity.

m23 at 0/1, 50 uL is predicted at 1.46/3.90 mL, unusually early relative to its measured 1/1 row 1a462e0cc4fc1474a76c at 100 uL. It tests the missing baseline of the rigid bicyclic acrylate after m18 strong-eluent predictions required correction in 68c511d842fc030aa84b. The amount difference remains explicit.

m46 at 0/1, 50 uL is predicted to finish at 9.12 mL, later than its measured 2/1 completion of 8.10 in 1e5f275917d54ddaf03b. This tests an uncovered baseline and whether the earlier endpoint-width artifact was accompanied by a distorted solvent-response shape.

m77 at 0/1, 50 uL establishes the missing baseline of the ethyl alpha-bromoester, predicted at 5.89/8.93 mL. Comparison with selected m46 and measured 2/1 row 3104197ca02407c049a3 helps learn ester-environment differences while retaining density and loading differences.

m77 at 1/1, 50 uL pairs with its selected pure-EA point. The predicted 7.46/9.36 response can teach its strong-side onset and completion separately. Existing 2/1 observations 3104197ca02407c049a3 and 308ffc82485e086c1c09 differ sharply across loading, including a nearly coincident-endpoint record, so transfer should be tested locally.

m81 at 0/1, 150 uL isolates loading in the baseline comparison with e301272fe83481e8a85d at 100 uL, measured at 4.27/14.64 mL. It also anchors the fixed-150-uL curve before the early completions measured at 1/1, 5/1 and 10/1. Prediction is 4.60/12.05.

m81 at 2/1, 150 uL fills the gap between measured 1/1 row 06c0c99f1cfb752ed34b and 5/1 row a9500e468002e41eceeb, which finish at 6.66 and 9.23 mL. Its predicted 12.98-mL completion tests another possible local maximum and gives a loading contrast against measured 50-uL row 36c9891cc52de490659d.

m117 at 1/1, 50 uL begins a matched lower-loading ratio pair. Measured 100-uL rows af0ec4f316723b99eaef and 5079d0dfcde65893b224 finish at 18.39 and 15.80 mL at 1/1 and 2/1. This label tests whether the observed completion decrease also occurs at 50 uL.

m117 at 2/1, 50 uL completes the selected lower-loading comparison, with predicted completion 16.20 versus 18.78 mL at 1/1. Unlike the rejected m127 peak prediction, a decrease is already measured at 100 uL; measuring this pair tests its reproducibility across amount.

m28 at 0/1, 50 uL tests whether its completion dependence on amount persists under pure EA. Measured 1/1 rows 686562279e2bfb73ef1e and 9845fd896eb72b0e149f finish at 12.50 and 19.96 mL at 50 and 150 uL. The pure-EA 150-uL reference cc1f4899902d6f44bef2 finishes at 13.61, close to this candidate's 13.56 prediction.

m185 at 0/1, 50 uL is predicted to finish at 16.15 mL, later than the same-loading 2/1 measurement f3a9b0a4924369149487 at 11.60. This is a direct test of a remaining strong-side reversal in an ortho-fluorinated aldehyde, where carbonyl environment could affect transfer but does not establish the predicted shape.

m117 at 2/1, 150 uL adds a second test of the completion dip, using measured 150-uL 1/1 and 5/1 references e55c8ef232b46d3a1ca9 and a0d6732883ffc7d063fb, which finish at 20.23 and 19.17 mL. Its predicted 16.41 completion tests persistence at higher loading and separates ratio shape from amount.

m63 at 0/1, 100 uL establishes the missing baseline after 06c1f0c9b81146ac92c4 measured a 5/1 completion of 13.93 mL. Measured m180 pure-EA row 1a3149e0c41e4560d347 provides a closely related fused-ketone reference. This tests whether their completion contrast persists toward pure EA.

m179 at 1/1, 100 uL expands the strong side of the larger-ring fused ketone, predicted at 6.42/11.22 mL. Its measured 10/1 and 50/1 anchors b6dc1ec0dbd724128ce3 and a36291cab664852df5e5 do not locate the initial response. This complements the recently corrected m63/m180 curves without assuming a constant ring-size offset.

m164 at 5/1, 100 uL tests where its large weak-eluent completion contrast with m165 emerges. Their measured 50/1 completions are 68.68 and 30.40 mL in c9bef93a79964dc6ede1 and 683b6279a87805548c7c, but selected 5/1 predictions differ by only about 1.45 mL. This locates a structural interaction along the response curve.

m165 at 5/1, 100 uL pairs with m164 under the same loading solvent and plug volume and nearly equal sample amounts. Prediction is 6.86/14.51 mL. Together with its measured 20/1 and 50/1 anchors a7f8c888870123f3b277 and 683b6279a87805548c7c, it tests whether the conjugation-dependent contrast appears before PE-rich conditions.

m164 at 2/1, 100 uL supplies the predecessor to its selected 5/1 point. Measured 1/1 row 3f6b817d855e67b3b406 finishes at 10.05 mL, while pure-EA row 5df546d9e2f2a29dfc89 finishes at 13.58. This tests the predicted recovery to 14.39 mL and constrains the strong-side shape independently of its late weak-eluent behavior.

m171 at 5/1, 100 uL adds a benzylic ketone comparison to the conjugated carbonyl selections. Only the supplied measured 1/1 and 50/1 anchors 0901fd8923d9679837cd and 3c358af26c2e2988cd46 constrain this graph's curve. The 5.99/11.98 prediction tests the intervening ordinary-volume regime.

m171 at 10/1, 100 uL forms a fixed-loading segment with its selected 5/1 row. Prediction rises to 7.23/15.94 mL before the measured 50/1 completion of 27.54 in 3c358af26c2e2988cd46. Two interior labels can distinguish gradual growth from a delayed response and improve transfer among aromatic ketone arrangements.

m68 at 5/1, 100 uL connects measured 2/1 row e3716bf7dba67a0f2185, finishing at 12.58 mL, to 20/1 row cb534927304d5c892100 at 17.50. Its predicted 17.21 completion places most of the rise before 5/1. This provides a biphenyl ketone boundary against spreading corrections from the more strongly responding conjugated graphs.

m16 at 2/1, 100 uL tests the stronger side of a predicted plateau: 7.36/11.39 mL is close to measured 20/1 row fd1f64e4a600c1da7a51 at 7.24/11.02. The label teaches whether a branched alkyl acrylate is already near that regime, complementing measured cyclic and long-chain acrylates.

m16 at 50/1, 100 uL supplies the weaker side of the same fixed-loading curve. Prediction is 9.03/14.43 mL, beyond its measured 20/1 response fd1f64e4a600c1da7a51. This pair tests plateau versus continued growth and helps distinguish alkyl environment from mobile-phase strength effects across acrylate rows.

m42 at 5/1, 50 uL fills a missing moderate-strength anchor below its measured 20/1 and 50/1 rows 840c35e5a30f05a5784c and cb42a00d7b000827217c. It pairs with selected para-fluoroacetophenone at the same sample volume, loading solvent and plug volume, providing a simple carbonyl comparison.

m34 at 5/1, 50 uL pairs with m42, with the density difference retained. Prediction is 6.89/14.94 mL. Measured m34 10/1 and 20/1 anchors 7fdf49a091a855c0138f and 122ecf89b68742b1bf36 establish a later response at higher PE; this tests whether the fluorine-associated contrast is already apparent at 5/1.

m189 at 0/1, 100 uL completes the missing baseline below its newly measured 1/1-to-5/1 segment. Rows 2c105d3b7f32d3b6a965, f1dafc187f7b1ec15297 and 5edaf16084f46f5b4726 finish at 13.68, 14.97 and 14.58 mL. This tests whether the plateau extends toward pure EA and broadens the measured polyaryl aldehyde response.

m33 at 1/1, 50 uL tests amount dependence beside measured 100-uL row 7a9775ac62acbc27a73d at 4.53/15.02 mL. Its predicted completion is only 11.25. Together with the selected pure-EA point, it tests whether elevated strong-side completion is loading-specific or a scaffold baseline that the predictor undertransfers.

m33 at 0/1, 50 uL pairs with its selected 1/1 row and permits a direct amount comparison with measured 100-uL pure-EA row 915cf3a7c8100cb7ce1f, finishing at 17.03 mL. The pair separates baseline loading effects from the solvent response of an ortho-substituted aromatic ketone.

m104 at 0/1, 50 uL establishes an uncovered anthranilate baseline, predicted at 4.87/10.18 mL. Recent 5/1 row ce103e949b7ef5641a1e finishes at 15.28, whereas identical-input 10/1 records disagree. A stronger-side anchor helps constrain this graph without encoding that disagreement as a general amount effect.

m104 at 1/1, 50 uL completes a fixed-loading 0/1-to-5/1 segment with the selected baseline and measured ce103e949b7ef5641a1e. The predicted 5.87/10.32 response tests where completion begins increasing and supports environment-specific aminoester transfer alongside measured ethyl anthranilate c41e4c2422a460476e8f.

m19 at 2/1, 50 uL tests the low-amount side of an ionizable acrylate response around measured 100-uL row 304fb0fdb486ae4b7a07 at 16.43/32.81 mL. The model predicts little amount dependence. Silica interactions make that a useful hypothesis to test, without assuming an amine loading rule from other scaffolds.

m19 at 2/1, 150 uL completes a three-level loading comparison using the selected 50-uL row and measured 304fb0fdb486ae4b7a07. Predicted endpoints remain near 15.99/33.89 mL. This tests the weak predicted amount sensitivity in a tertiary amine environment and provides a boundary against transferring m212's pronounced 5/1 loading response.

hypotheses.content: Several previously predicted strong-eluent reversals or endpoint distortions were model artifacts. Remaining unusual baselines warrant targeted labels, but the evidence supports compound-specific response repair rather than a universal monotonicity constraint.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Missing strong-eluent labels can correct onset, completion and response shape across many ordinary-volume rows, including cases whose numerical diagnostics are modest.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m185 actually finish later under pure EA than at 2/1 at fixed loading, and do the missing m23, m46 and m77 baselines reproduce their predicted early or reversed responses?

hypotheses.content: The nearly coincident m62 endpoints at 1/1 and 150 uL could be isolated label behavior or a reproducible ratio feature. The current predictor transfers the elevated onset to 50 uL, but that transfer has no measured confirmation.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Testing a different loading can prevent one unusual observation from becoming a graph-wide ratio feature, or establish a genuine conditional response if it reproduces.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 50 uL, does the matched 0/1-to-1/1 comparison reproduce the large onset increase and short 1/1 elution interval?

hypotheses.content: m81 completion depends on the combination of ratio and amount. The new 20/1, 100-uL completion agrees closely with its 50/1 value, while 10/1 completion at 150 uL is much earlier than at 50 uL. A common completion increase or global amount correction is therefore inadequate.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Fixed-amount strong-side labels can separate baseline loading dependence from ratio curvature and constrain completion independently of the consistently early onset.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 150 uL, how do the missing pure-EA and 2/1 completions connect the measured 1/1 and 5/1 responses?

hypotheses.content: At 100 uL, m117 finishes earlier at 2/1 than at 1/1: 15.80 versus 18.39 mL. Persistence of this completion decrease at other amounts is unknown. It provides an observed counterexample to treating every strong-side reversal as a prediction artifact.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A matched lower-loading pair and a higher-loading 2/1 point distinguish a reproducible response shape from an amount-specific or unexplained deviation.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the 1/1-to-2/1 completion decrease reproduce at 50 uL, and is 2/1 also earlier than the measured 1/1 and 5/1 completions at 150 uL?

hypotheses.content: Polyaryl carbonyl arrangements have different solvent-response shapes. The measured m164-minus-m165 completion contrast is large at 50/1, while their current 5/1 predictions are close. The ratio at which that contrast develops remains unmeasured; aromaticity or carbonyl count alone cannot locate it.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Intermediate-ratio comparisons teach where conjugation, carbonyl placement and aromatic arrangement alter retention, while ordinary-response controls limit excessive transfer from late-eluting graphs.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are m164 and m165 already different at 5/1, and do m171 and m68 show gradual growth or an early completion plateau over their missing interior segments?

hypotheses.content: A persistent earlier-onset effect of the 400-uL DCM plug across amounts is weakened. The 50/1 onset contrast is 4.28 mL at 50 uL sample volume but only 0.21 mL at 100 uL; the 20/1 contrast at 50 uL is also small. An amount-specific interaction or unexplained variation remains plausible.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: This prevents the earlier 50-uL contrast from motivating a global plug-volume correction and lowers the priority of additional nearby configuration labels.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Would another fixed-amount 50/1 configuration comparison reproduce the original low-loading onset difference? This is deferred in favor of missing response segments.

feedback_interpretation: The latest labels strengthen the case for repairing specific response artifacts: m49's pure-EA endpoints were ordered, m127 did not have the predicted 1/1 completion maximum, and m62, m80 and m74 had earlier pure-EA completions than predicted. However, m62's measured 1/1 endpoints nearly coincide at 12.24/12.26 mL, so a blanket monotonicity correction would be unjustified. I now test its transfer across loading and contrast it with m117's independently observed completion decrease. The m46 low-loading interval was also wider than predicted, supporting separate attention to both endpoints. The m168 configuration hypothesis weakened substantially: the new 100-uL 50/1 onset is almost identical between plug volumes, and the 20/1 onset contrast is small. Further nearby plug comparisons receive lower priority. For m81, the new 20/1, 100-uL completion of 17.62 mL essentially matches its 50/1 value of 17.86, while the 150-uL 10/1 completion is only 9.74; I replace a broad completion-rise interpretation with a conditional ratio-by-amount question. The alcohol onset contrast shrank from 8.72 mL at 5/1 to 1.01 mL at 1/1, supporting the proposed ratio-dependent contrast and reducing the need for another adjacent pair. Ring-N baselines are distinct: low-loading m216 retains a 22.49-mL completion under pure EA, whereas m146 finishes at 17.55; m211's 2/1 completions of 13.44 and 15.82 were substantially earlier than predicted. These measurements already constrain several nearby gaps. Low-loading m72 in PE agreed closely with its DCM references, and the m9 solvent control also agreed, weakening any universal loading-configuration correction. Finally, the m189 plateau, higher-than-predicted fused-ketone completions, and the measured m128/m129 contrast favor additional ordinary-volume carbonyl response segments rather than concentrating only on historically extreme errors.
batch_rationale: The 32 labels form interpretable local experiments with measured boundaries. The m62 pair tests whether an unusual label has become an unjustified transferable feature; the m117 comparisons test whether a measured reversal persists across amount. m81, m28, m33 and m19 address conditional loading responses, with unchanged recorded configurations within each comparison. Missing baselines for acrylates, bromoesters, aldehydes and anthranilate constrain where strong-eluent corrections should and should not transfer. The polyaryl and fused-ketone selections locate structural contrasts along response curves, while m16 and the acetophenone comparison cover common ordinary-volume relationships. Multiple selections on a molecule resolve a ratio segment or loading contrast; identical-condition duplicates were not selected incidentally. Further m72/m92 repeats and m168 plug comparisons were deprioritized because existing variation and the newest matched outcomes reduce their expected marginal value. This batch may improve overall Row-distribution accuracy by learning structure-condition interactions and separate onset/completion behavior across recurring chemical families, rather than maximizing retention or predicted error. Quantile widths are single-predictor diagnostics, not calibrated epistemic uncertainty, and V2 minus V1 is the elution interval. All 32 IDs and their supplied full-precision premeasurement predictions are frozen jointly before any new label reveal.
